comparison: Both evaluate ICD-related subtypes and survival associations (C14-C21) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence with statistical significance. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as a strength but characterize the evidence as 'potential but weak' within methodological limitations.

Major disagreement on immune infiltration analyses (C22-C29). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with multiple complementary analyses. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, citing 'inherent methodological limitations' of bulk RNA-Seq and inability to distinguish cell subsets accurately, recommending single-cell sequencing for reliability.

Disagreement on immunotherapy response findings (C30-C33, C106). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with consistent evidence patterns. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, calling findings 'intriguing' but emphasizing they are based on retrospective analyses with limited clinical detail requiring prospective validation.

Both evaluate the risk model construction (C34-C37, C101, C103) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes methodological soundness and reproducibility. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as a major strength but characterize clinical guidance as 'potential but weak,' indicating acceptance with reservations about strength.

Both evaluate mutation and TMB findings (C38-C41) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes internal consistency and biological interpretation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these as part of multi-dimensional data integration without raising specific concerns.

Both evaluate gene expression and risk associations (C45-C48, C73-C76) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes internal consistency. Peer reviewers acknowledge tissue array validation as a strength, though within context of overall 'potential but weak clinical guidance.'

Both evaluate clinical correlations and prognostic value (C49-C57) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval honestly reports modest AUC values while establishing independent prognostic value. Peer reviewers accept these as part of multi-dimensional validation supporting clinical applicability.

Partial overlap on subgroup analyses. OpenEval R8 covers C55-C57 (subgroup stratification) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R7 includes these claims within broader clinical associations, also rated SUPPORTED, acknowledging stage-specific effects.

Disagreement on immune profiling evidence (C58-C65, C102). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with comprehensive convergent evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, citing bulk RNA-Seq methodological limitations and emphasizing need for robust single-cell sequencing to enhance reliability.

Both evaluate drug sensitivity predictions (C66-C67) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval cites unclear methodology and lack of validation. Peer reviewers question 'unexpected correlations' needing mechanistic validation, cautioning about indirect associations versus direct biological relevance.

Disagreement on immunotherapy stratification (C68-C69). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting consistency with immune exhaustion phenotype. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, calling findings 'intriguing' but requiring prospective studies with detailed patient characterization for robust confirmation.

Both evaluate tissue microarray validation (C70-C72, C77) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes modest but adequate sample size with TCGA-tissue consistency. Peer reviewers acknowledge tissue array validation as a strength, though overall clinical guidance remains 'potential but weak.'

Disagreement on tissue correlations with immune markers (C78-C82, C98). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with correlation analyses. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, applying concerns about bulk RNA-Seq limitations and emphasizing need for single-cell sequencing despite tissue microarray data.

Both evaluate single-cell expression patterns (C83-C86, C100) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes mechanistic insights from cell-type-specific patterns. Peer reviewers acknowledge preliminary single-cell data addresses bulk RNA-seq concerns, accepting as supporting evidence despite being preliminary.

Disagreement on mechanistic interpretations (C87-C92 and overlapping claims). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with literature integration and acknowledged paradoxes. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether genes are ICD-specific versus general immune-response genes, requiring clearer biological validation.

Disagreement on synthesis and model interpretation (C93-C97, C99). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with coherent model from immune data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN (within R15), questioning ICD-specificity versus broader immune processes and requiring clearer biological implications.

Both evaluate IL1R1 fibroblast expression (C100) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites single-cell data and literature. Peer reviewers include this within preliminary single-cell validation, accepting as part of cell-type-specific evidence.

Partial overlap on summary conclusions. OpenEval R18 covers C102-C105 rated SUPPORTED. Peer R4 includes C103 (model utility) within broader model evaluation, rated SUPPORTED but with 'potential but weak' characterization.

Partial overlap on C102 (TME evaluation). OpenEval R18 includes this in summary conclusions rated SUPPORTED. Peer R8 addresses related immune profiling claims rated UNCERTAIN due to methodological limitations.

Partial overlap on C104-C105 (nuanced ICD interpretation). OpenEval R18 rates SUPPORTED as well-supported summary. Peer R15 rates UNCERTAIN, questioning ICD-specificity and requiring clearer distinction from general immune responses.

Both evaluate background/context claims (C1-C13) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are properly cited literature establishing rationale. Peer reviewers accept these foundational statements without question as standard background.
